title: The query-log conflict scenario passes on the Windows CI job
goal: _tools/test_querylog_e2e.py::TestConflict passes on the kb-tests-windows job: the querylog/<run-id> branch holds the gap entry and main does not after the second run, with the cause fixed where it lies (test or ql_deliver) and a test that reproduces it on any OS.

gates.question: The cause needs one Windows CI run that tells (a) from (b). Which experiment?
options: In TestConflict.scenario keep the branch's and main1's _gaps.md after the first run and the `said` lines of both distills; split line 698 into branch-vs-main1 (the entry reached the branch) and main-after-again-vs-main1 (the held entry stayed off main), each with the said lines as its message; run kb-tests-windows with -k TestConflict
Keep the scenario's temporary directory on the Windows job and upload e2e-conflict0 as a job artifact, then read the remote's refs and the worktree's findings files by hand
gates.recommendation: The first: a stricter, self-describing assertion that stays in the suite; one -k TestConflict Windows run names the failing half, which is then reproduced on any OS with a planted condition and fixed

notes: Cause not pinned. The failing assertion (test_querylog_e2e.py:698) found the querylog/<run-id> branch's kb/public/_gaps.md EQUAL to main's, not different past the shown prefix: pytest shows `assert (a != b)` failing, and World.show reads git in text mode, so line endings can neither make nor hide a difference; the gap entry is on neither ref or on both. w.show(GAPS) reads main after the second distill (`again`), not main1. Two readings: (a) the first run's branch commit lacks the gap entry (apply wrote none, or it was not committed); (b) the second run applied the held gap on main (held() found nothing, or apply ignored --hold). Against (a): TestResearch, which applies the same `gap` lookup on an unchanged kb, passes on the same job. Against (b): held() and --hold are plain git and argv code. Ruled out on macOS: git 2.56.0 built from source (the job's MinGit version) passes the scenario; test_querylog, test_querylog_e2e, test_sync and test_research_merge under -n 2 --dist loadscope pass; no tool or test sets os.environ in process; every file the pipeline writes uses newline="\n" under `* text=auto eol=lf`. A local Windows 11 run (Git for Windows 2.55, 8 workers) passed this test; the CI job (MinGit 2.56.0, 2 workers, container user) fails it on every run.
